english: I wish I had time to make more show pieces, but Adeline keeps me so busy making nails and joints...
french: J'aimerais concevoir plus de pièces de collection, mais je passe mon temps à fabriquer des clous et des rivets pour Adeline...
russian: Жаль, что не хватает времени делать больше показных изделий, но Аделина всё время загружает меня гвоздями и крепежами...
bulgarian: I wish I had time to make more show pieces, but Adeline keeps me so busy making nails and joints...

english: I'd rather people carry on the smithing tradition.
french: J'aime que les gens perpétuent la tradition de la forge.
russian: Главное, чтобы кузнечное ремесло не исчезло.
bulgarian: I'd rather people carry on the smithing tradition.

english: I don't mind if you use my anvil to make the same tools that I'm selling.
french: Tu peux te servir de l'enclume pour créer des outils identiques à ceux que je vends.
russian: Мне не жалко, если ты используешь мою наковальню, даже если делаешь те же инструменты, что и я продаю.
bulgarian: I don't mind if you use my anvil to make the same tools that I'm selling.

english: It's not often I'm away from the forge... there's always more to do.
french: Je ne sors pas très souvent de la forge... Il y a toujours quelque chose à faire.
russian: Я не так часто отхожу от кузницы... Работы там всегда хватает.
bulgarian: It's not often I'm away from the forge... there's always more to do.

english: Balor buys a lot of replacement parts for his wagon from me and Ryis... what's he get up to, I wonder? And where does he get all that rare ore?
french: Balor achète souvent des pièces de rechange pour son chariot auprès de Ryis et moi... Je me demande ce qu'il en fait. Et où est-ce qu'il trouve tous ces minerais rares ?
russian: Балор часто покупает у меня и Риза запчасти для своего фургона... Интересно, чем он там занимается? И где он берёт такую редкую руду?
bulgarian: Balor buys a lot of replacement parts for his wagon from me and Ryis... what's he get up to, I wonder? And where does he get all that rare ore?

english: Baron Wiscar really knows his stuff, he could have been a blacksmith if he hadn't been granted peerage by the king.
french: Le baron Wiscar est vraiment doué. Il aurait pu devenir forgeron s'il n'avait pas été anobli par le roi.
russian: Барон Вискар отлично разбирается в кузнечестве. Мог бы стать мастером, если бы король не дал ему титул.
bulgarian: Baron Wiscar really knows his stuff, he could have been a blacksmith if he hadn't been granted peerage by the king.

english: Oh, hey.
french: Tiens, bonjour.
russian: А, это ты.
bulgarian: Oh, hey.

english: Hey.
french: Salut.
russian: Привет.
bulgarian: Hey.

english: What, did you need something?
french: Quoi ? Tu as besoin de quelque chose ?
russian: Что, нужно что-то?
bulgarian: What, did you need something?

english: Hey.
french: Salut.
russian: Привет.
bulgarian: Hey.

english: Morning.
french: Bonjour.
russian: Доброе утро.
bulgarian: Morning.

english: What's up?
french: Quoi de neuf ?
russian: Как оно?
bulgarian: What's up?

english: Hm? Oh, hey [Ari].
french: Mmm ? Oh, salut [Ari].
russian: М? А, привет, [Ari].
bulgarian: Hm? Oh, hey [Ari].

english: Hey [Ari].
french: Salut, [Ari].
russian: Эй, [Ari].
bulgarian: Hey [Ari].

english: Oh!
french: Oh !
russian: О!
bulgarian: Oh!

english: I feel refreshed.
french: C'est très revigorant.
russian: Освежился.
bulgarian: I feel refreshed.

english: The bath feels amazing after a day spent hammering away at the forge. Whew.
french: J'adore venir aux bains après une journée passée à travailler le métal. Pfiou.
russian: После дня у горна ванна — просто спасение. Фух.
bulgarian: The bath feels amazing after a day spent hammering away at the forge. Whew.

english: A hot bath always relaxes my muscles...
french: Un bain chaud me détend les muscles...
russian: Горячая вода хорошо расслабляет мышцы...
bulgarian: A hot bath always relaxes my muscles...

english: Then I can get back to work.
french: Et je peux retourner travailler.
russian: Потом можно снова за работу.
bulgarian: Then I can get back to work.

english: Sometimes I wake up with a tense neck, and that's when I come over here.
french: Je me réveille parfois avec le cou tout raide, donc je viens ici.
russian: Иногда просыпаюсь с зажатой шеей — тогда и иду сюда.
bulgarian: Sometimes I wake up with a tense neck, and that's when I come over here.

english: I thought my hands were going to smell like copper all day, but a bath really did the trick.
french: Je pensais que mes mains allaient sentir le cuivre pendant toute la journée, mais le bain m'a débarrassé de l'odeur.
russian: Думал, руки весь день будут вонять медью, но ванна и с этим справилась.
bulgarian: I thought my hands were going to smell like copper all day, but a bath really did the trick.

english: Good bath.
french: Un bon bain, c'est très agréable.
russian: Хорошая ванна.
bulgarian: Good bath.

english: Seems like a lot of work.
french: Ça demande sûrement beaucoup de travail.
russian: Наверное, с этим много возни.
bulgarian: Seems like a lot of work.

english: It always smells nice in the Bathhouse, but it also smells different every time?
french: Ça sent toujours bon, aux bains, mais l'odeur change chaque jour.
russian: В купальне всегда приятно пахнет, но каждый раз по-новому...
bulgarian: It always smells nice in the Bathhouse, but it also smells different every time?

english: When I asked Juniper, she smirked and said it was magic. Ugh.
french: Quand j'ai demandé à Juniper, elle a souri et elle a dit que c'était de la magie. Pfff.
russian: Когда я спросил Джунипер, она ухмыльнулась и сказала: «магия». Тьфу.
bulgarian: When I asked Juniper, she smirked and said it was magic. Ugh.

english: I wonder what keeps the water at the Bathhouse hot all the time.
french: Je me demande comment l'eau est tout le temps chaude aux bains.
russian: Интересно, за счёт чего поддерживается температура воды в купальне.
bulgarian: I wonder what keeps the water at the Bathhouse hot all the time.

english: Got another early day tomorrow.
french: Je me lève de bonne heure, demain.
russian: А завтра пораньше снова пойду работать.
bulgarian: Got another early day tomorrow.

english: A quick bath, and then bed for me.
french: Un petit bain, et je vais me coucher.
russian: Искупаться по-быстрому — и в постель.
bulgarian: A quick bath, and then bed for me.

english: W-what? I didn't say I was going to try it!
french: Q-Quoi ? Je n'ai pas dit que j'allais essayer !
russian: Ч-что? Я не говорил, что собираюсь это делать!
bulgarian: W-what? I didn't say I was going to try it!

english: You know, sand can be turned to glass at extremely high temperatures...
french: Tu sais, à très haute température, le sable se transforme en verre...
russian: Знаешь, песок можно превратить в стекло при очень высокой температуре...
bulgarian: You know, sand can be turned to glass at extremely high temperatures...

english: I know you can't help staring, but can you do it from further away?
french: Je vois bien que tu ne peux pas t'empêcher de regarder, mais tu peux t'éloigner un peu ?
russian: Понимаю, что трудно не пялиться, но ты можешь делать это издалека?
bulgarian: I know you can't help staring, but can you do it from further away?

english: So friendly.
french: Très amicale...
russian: Очень дружеское.
bulgarian: So friendly.

english: Ryis and I are having a shell-collecting competition. It's friendly.
french: Ryis et moi, on fait un concours pour voir qui ramassera le plus de coquillages. Une compétition amicale.
russian: Мы с Ризом устроили соревнование: кто больше ракушек соберёт. Дружеское.
bulgarian: Ryis and I are having a shell-collecting competition. It's friendly.

english: What do you want, [Ari]?
french: Tu veux quelque chose, [Ari] ?
russian: Чего хочешь, [Ari]?
bulgarian: What do you want, [Ari]?

english: Making yourself at home, I see.
french: Je vois que tu te fais comme chez toi.
russian:
Устроились

УстроиласьУстроилсяУстроилось тут, смотрю.
bulgarian: Making yourself at home, I see.

english: So this is how we're starting your second year in Mistria, huh?
french: Alors c'est comme ça que tu commences ta deuxième année à Mistria, hein ?
russian: Вот так ты начинаешь свой второй год в Мистрии, да?
bulgarian: So this is how we're starting your second year in Mistria, huh?

english: Shop's closed, [Ari]. In case you were confused about that.
french: La boutique est fermée, [Ari]. Au cas où tu n'aurais pas compris.
russian:
Магазин закрыт, [Ari], если ты не

заметили

заметилазаметилзаметило.
bulgarian: Shop's closed, [Ari]. In case you were confused about that.

english: H-hey, [Ari]...
french: S-Salut, [Ari]...
russian: П-привет, [Ari]...
bulgarian: H-hey, [Ari]...

english: Um. Whatever it is, can it wait till tomorrow, [Ari]?
french: Euh. Je ne sais pas ce que tu veux, mais est-ce que ça peut attendre demain, [Ari] ?
russian: Эм. Если ты по делу, может оно подождать до завтра, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Um. Whatever it is, can it wait till tomorrow, [Ari]?

english: Hemlock's an excellent bartender. I haven't had better =Beer=, even in the Capital.
french: Hemlock est un gérant de taverne hors pair. Je n'avais jamais bu de =bière= aussi bonne, même à la capitale.
russian: Хемлок отличный бармен. Даже в столице такого =пива= не пил.
bulgarian: Hemlock's an excellent bartender. I haven't had better =Beer=, even in the Capital.

english: What is it? I've got a big work order to get through.
french: Qu'est-ce qu'il y a ? J'ai une commande très importante à honorer.
russian: Чего тебе? У меня большой заказ, надо успеть.
bulgarian: What is it? I've got a big work order to get through.

english: I've got half a mind to skip dinner and put some time in at the forge... but Olric says dinner is our sacred bro time.
french: J'ai parfois envie de sauter le dîner pour continuer à travailler à la forge... mais Olric tient à ce moment sacré entre frères.
russian: Вот думаю: может, пропустить ужин и пойти поработать... но Ольрик говорит, ужин — это священное время для братанов.
bulgarian: I've got half a mind to skip dinner and put some time in at the forge... but Olric says dinner is our sacred bro time.

english: Blacksmithing is hard work, but it does burn through a lot of energy. A bar of =Chocolate= is a good boost.
french: Travailler le métal est difficile et demande beaucoup d'énergie. Un peu de =chocolat= permet de récupérer ses forces.
russian: Кузнечное дело тяжёлое, зато энергии сжигает много. Плитка =шоколада= — хороший заряд.
bulgarian: Blacksmithing is hard work, but it does burn through a lot of energy. A bar of =Chocolate= is a good boost.

english: Let Hemlock pick a brew for you. He always gets it right.
french: Demande à Hemlock de te conseiller. Il fait toujours le bon choix.
russian: Дай Хемлоку выбрать тебе сорт. Он всегда угадывает.
bulgarian: Let Hemlock pick a brew for you. He always gets it right.

english: A cold =Beer= hits different after a long day of work.
french: Après une longue journée de travail, rien ne vaut une bonne =bière= bien fraîche.
russian: Холодное =пиво= после рабочего дня — совсем другое дело.
bulgarian: A cold =Beer= hits different after a long day of work.

english: Nothing better than a cold drink after working on a hot summer's day.
french: Une boisson bien fraîche après une chaude journée d'été, il n'y a que ça de vrai.
russian: Нет ничего лучше холодного напитка после жаркой кузни.
bulgarian: Nothing better than a cold drink after working on a hot summer's day.

english: Sometimes Eiland asks me to make replicas of old artifacts... I thought it was boring at first, but the ancients actually have a lot to teach about working metal.
french: Je fais parfois des reproductions d'artéfacts anciens pour Eiland... Je trouvais ça ennuyeux au début, mais j'apprends beaucoup de la façon dont les anciens travaillaient le métal.
russian: Иногда Эйланд просит сделать копии старых артефактов... Сначала скучно было, а потом понял: у древних есть чему поучиться в обработке металла.
bulgarian: Sometimes Eiland asks me to make replicas of old artifacts... I thought it was boring at first, but the ancients actually have a lot to teach about working metal.

english: Just taking care of a few things around town.
french: J'ai quelques commissions à faire en ville.
russian: Просто по делам хожу по городу.
bulgarian: Just taking care of a few things around town.

english: I keep having to remind him that other folks need eggs too.
french: Je dois toujours lui rappeler qu'il n'est pas le seul à aimer les œufs.
russian: Приходится напоминать ему, что яйца нужны не только ему.
bulgarian: I keep having to remind him that other folks need eggs too.

english: Olric asked me to pick up five dozen $Eggs$ while I was at the store...
french: Comme j'allais faire quelques courses, Olric m'a demandé de lui rapporter cinq douzaines d'$œufs$...
russian: Ольрик попросил купить пять десятков $яиц$, пока я в лавке...
bulgarian: Olric asked me to pick up five dozen $Eggs$ while I was at the store...

english: Hmm. Excuse me.
french: Hmm. Pardon.
russian: Хмм. Прошу прощения.
bulgarian: Hmm. Excuse me.

english: Must be nice, working in something as forgiving as farming. You can't play around when you're working with molten metal.
french: Ça doit être sympa l'agriculture. Même si tu te trompes, ce n'est pas bien grave. Avec du métal en fusion, on n'a pas le droit à l'erreur.
russian: Здорово, наверное, заниматься таким простеньким делом, как фермерство. А вот с расплавленным металом дурака особо не поваляешь.
bulgarian: Must be nice, working in something as forgiving as farming. You can't play around when you're working with molten metal.

english: It'll be hard to keep up on my work if it stays this cold.
french: Cela va être difficile de garder la cadence si ce froid continue.
russian: Если и дальше будет так холодно, с работой будет сложно.
bulgarian: It'll be hard to keep up on my work if it stays this cold.

english: It was a battle to get the fire going earlier.
french: Mon feu a eu du mal à prendre, tout à l'heure.
russian: Разжечь огонь сегодня было настоящим испытанием.
bulgarian: It was a battle to get the fire going earlier.

english: Not now, [Ari]. Concentrating. I have to get this done if I want to make it to the Inn later.
french: Pas maintenant, [Ari]. Je suis concentré. Je dois terminer ce que je suis en train de faire si je veux pouvoir aller à l'auberge plus tard.
russian: Не сейчас, [Ari]. Я сосредоточен. Надо закончить, если хочу успеть в трактир.
bulgarian: Not now, [Ari]. Concentrating. I have to get this done if I want to make it to the Inn later.

english: I'm all fired up! Let's make some nails!
french: Je suis chaud comme la braise ! J'ai des tas de clous à fabriquer !
russian: Ух, я раскочегарился! Сейчас наделаю гвоздей!
bulgarian: I'm all fired up! Let's make some nails!

english: There's nothing better than working the forge in fall. Taste that crisp air!
french: L'automne est ma saison préférée pour travailler à la forge. Il y a toujours un petit courant d'air rafraîchissant !
russian: Осенью ковать на воздухе — самое приятное дело. Такая свежесть в каждом вдохе!
bulgarian: There's nothing better than working the forge in fall. Taste that crisp air!

english: I like working the forge in autumn. The chill in the air makes it pretty cozy.
french: J'aime bien travailler à la forge en automne. L'air frais crée une ambiance apaisante.
russian: Осенью у горна работать приятно. Прохлада делает всё уютнее.
bulgarian: I like working the forge in autumn. The chill in the air makes it pretty cozy.

english: Hard to keep the forge fire going on rainy days...
french: C'est difficile de faire prendre les braises les jours de pluie.
russian: В дождь тяжело поддерживать пламя в горне...
bulgarian: Hard to keep the forge fire going on rainy days...

english: You'll get burned if you're careless.
french: Tu pourrais te brûler si tu ne fais pas attention.
russian:
Будешь

неосторожны

неосторожнанеостороженнеосторожно, обожжёшься
bulgarian: You'll get burned if you're careless.

english: Hey, watch yourself around the forge.
french: Hé, sois prudent<he></he><she>e</she><they>·e</they> près de la forge.
russian: Эй, поосторожней у горна.
bulgarian: Hey, watch yourself around the forge.

english: There's no escaping this heat when there's work to be done.
french: Avec toutes les commandes en cours, il faut savoir résister à la chaleur.
russian: Пока работа не сделана, от этой жары никуда не денешься.
bulgarian: There's no escaping this heat when there's work to be done.

english: Whew...
french: Pfiou...
russian: Уф...
bulgarian: Whew...

english: He's not allowed to do that any more.
french: Je lui ai ordonné d'arrêter.
russian: Теперь ему это запрещено.
bulgarian: He's not allowed to do that any more.

english: Olric used to do jumping jacks next to the forge as part of his morning workout.
french: Olric avait pour habitude de faire ses exercices matinaux juste à côté de la forge.
russian: Ольрик раньше делал зарядку возле горна: прыжки, там, всякие.
bulgarian: Olric used to do jumping jacks next to the forge as part of his morning workout.

english: Sorry, can't stop now... I've got to finish shaping the metal before it cools off.
french: Désolé, mais je ne peux pas m'interrompre maintenant... Je dois donner sa forme à ce métal avant qu'il ne refroidisse.
russian: Прости, не могу отвлечься... нужно закончить, пока металл не остыл.
bulgarian: Sorry, can't stop now... I've got to finish shaping the metal before it cools off.

english: You can watch, but leave me some elbow room.
french: Tu peux rester regarder, mais laisse-moi un peu de place pour travailler.
russian: Можешь смотреть, но оставь мне место для локтей.
bulgarian: You can watch, but leave me some elbow room.

english: So I've got to work hard too.
french: Donc moi aussi, je dois travailler dur.
russian: Так что и мне надо не отставать.
bulgarian: So I've got to work hard too.

english: Olric always works hard...
french: Olric travaille toujours d'arrache-pied...
russian: Ольрик всегда пашет как вол...
bulgarian: Olric always works hard...

english: Just give me a few to finish this up.
french: Laisse-moi un peu de temps pour finir ça.
russian: Дай мне немного времени, пока я закончу.
bulgarian: Just give me a few to finish this up.

english: Oh, sorry [Ari]...
french: Oh, désolé, [Ari]...
russian: Ой, прости, [Ari]...
bulgarian: Oh, sorry [Ari]...

english: Come here, you can warm up by the forge.
french: Viens te réchauffer près de la forge.
russian: Иди сюда, можешь погреться у печи.
bulgarian: Come here, you can warm up by the forge.

english: Are you cold, [Ari]?
french: Tu as froid, [Ari] ?
russian: Тебе не холодно, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Are you cold, [Ari]?

english: I guess I better hurry things up.
french: Il va falloir que je mette les bouchées doubles.
russian: Видимо, придётся поднажать.
bulgarian: I guess I better hurry things up.

english: Ah... This order is taking longer than I meant to.
french: Ah... Cette commande me prend plus de temps que prévu.
russian: Эх... Я вожусь с этим заказом дольше, чем рассчитывал.
bulgarian: Ah... This order is taking longer than I meant to.

english: But I'm not a fan of having to clear it off my anvil.
french: Mais je n'aime pas quand je dois nettoyer mon enclume après coup.
russian: Но счищать его с наковальни я не люблю.
bulgarian: But I'm not a fan of having to clear it off my anvil.

english: It's nice, watching a fresh snow fall...
french: J'adore regarder la neige tomber...
russian: Приятно наблюдать за снегопадом...
bulgarian: It's nice, watching a fresh snow fall...

english: Maybe that's his way of apologizing for Adeline's bulk nail requests.
french: C'est peut-être une manière de s'excuser pour les grosses commandes de clous d'Adeline.
russian: Может, таким образом он хочет извиниться за массовые заказы на гвозди от Аделины.
bulgarian: Maybe that's his way of apologizing for Adeline's bulk nail requests.

english: Eiland is always bringing me interesting little projects to work on.
french: Eiland me propose toujours des petits projets intéressants.
russian: Эйланд всегда приносит мне новые интересные проекты.
bulgarian: Eiland is always bringing me interesting little projects to work on.

english: She thinks I'm an artist? Nice to be recognized.
french: Elle me prend pour un artiste ? Ça fait plaisir de se sentir reconnu.
russian: Выходит, она считает меня художником? Приятно, когда признают талант.
bulgarian: She thinks I'm an artist? Nice to be recognized.

english: Elsie said she likes to bring me projects because she's a patron of the arts.
french: Elsie a dit qu'elle aimait me soumettre des projets parce que c'est une amatrice d'art.
russian: Элси сказала, что она даёт мне заказы, потому что любит покровительствовать искусству.
bulgarian: Elsie said she likes to bring me projects because she's a patron of the arts.

english: At breathing down my neck when I'm working?
french: ... Pour me déranger quand je suis en plein travail ?
russian: В стоянии у меня за спиной, пока я работаю?
bulgarian: At breathing down my neck when I'm working?

english: Hmm, is it just me or are you getting more skilled-
french: Mmm, c'est moi ou tu commences à être doué<she>e</she><he></he><they>·e</they>...
russian: Хмм, или мне кажется, или ты становишься всё искуснее...
bulgarian: Hmm, is it just me or are you getting more skilled-

english: Want to give me a hand here? You'll warm up in no time.
french: Ça te dirait de me donner un coup de main ? Tu te réchaufferas en un clin d'œil.
russian: Хочешь со мной поработать? Мигом согреешься.
bulgarian: Want to give me a hand here? You'll warm up in no time.

english: Are you cold, [Ari]?
french: Tu as froid, [Ari] ?
russian:
Не

замёрзли

замёрзлазамёрззамёрзло, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Are you cold, [Ari]?

english: You can watch, but mind the sparks.
french: Tu peux regarder, mais attention aux étincelles.
russian: Можешь посмотреть, только осторожно: искры летят.
bulgarian: You can watch, but mind the sparks.

english: You can watch, but mind the sparks.
french: Tu peux regarder, mais attention aux étincelles.
russian: Можешь посмотреть, только осторожно: искры летят.
bulgarian: You can watch, but mind the sparks.

english: But you better clean up after yourself.
french: Mais pense bien à tout nettoyer ensuite.
russian: Но не забудь убрать за собой.
bulgarian: But you better clean up after yourself.

english: I'll let you use the forge if you need it...
french: Je t'autorise à utiliser la forge quand tu veux...
russian: Можешь воспользоваться горном, если нужно...
bulgarian: I'll let you use the forge if you need it...

english: Don't stand too close... I'm trying to work here.
french: N'approche pas trop... J'essaie de travailler.
russian: Не стой так близко... Я, вообще-то, работаю.
bulgarian: Don't stand too close... I'm trying to work here.

english: The contrast is nice.
french: J'aime bien ce contraste.
russian: Такой контраст приятно ощущать.
bulgarian: The contrast is nice.

english: It's warm by the forge on a cold day.
french: Quand il fait froid, on peut se réchauffer près du fourneau.
russian: В холодный день у горна всё равно тепло.
bulgarian: It's warm by the forge on a cold day.

english: You can warm up by the forge, if you want.
french: Si tu veux, tu peux venir te réchauffer près du fourneau.
russian: Если хочешь, можешь погреться у горна.
bulgarian: You can warm up by the forge, if you want.

english: Aren't you cold, standing around like that?
french: Tu n'as pas froid à rester là sans rien faire ?
russian: Тебе не холодно вот так просто стоять?
bulgarian: Aren't you cold, standing around like that?

english: It's best to get forge work in early, before the day's heat sets in.
french: Il vaut mieux se mettre à travailler le métal tôt le matin, avant que n'arrive la chaleur accablante de la journée.
russian: Лучше ковать с утра, пока дневная жара не набрала силу.
bulgarian: It's best to get forge work in early, before the day's heat sets in.

english: The temperature inside the forge has been steady today.
french: La température est restée constante à la forge aujourd'hui.
russian: Температура в горне сегодня держится ровно.
bulgarian: The temperature inside the forge has been steady today.

english: So don't distract me.
french: Ne va pas me déranger.
russian: Так что не отвлекай.
bulgarian: So don't distract me.

english: Keeping the heat even requires a lot of concentration.
french: Il faut beaucoup de concentration pour maintenir une chaleur constante.
russian: Удерживать тепло — дело не простое, требует сосредоточенности.
bulgarian: Keeping the heat even requires a lot of concentration.

english: A book on how to deal with difficult people.
french: Un livre pour gérer les gens pénibles.
russian: Да, книгу «Как справляться с трудными людьми».
bulgarian: A book on how to deal with difficult people.

english: I'm not trying to be funny! Get out!
french: Ce n'était pas le but ! Va-t'en !
russian: Я не шучу! Уходи!
bulgarian: I'm not trying to be funny! Get out!

english: Do you uh, normally come into people's rooms uninvited? Is that a thing where you're from?
french: Euh, ça t'arrive souvent de débarquer dans la chambre de quelqu'un sans prévenir ? C'est une coutume d'où tu viens ?
russian: Ты, эээ, часто вот так заходишь в чужие комнаты без стука? У вас там это нормально?
bulgarian: Do you uh, normally come into people's rooms uninvited? Is that a thing where you're from?

english: What are you reading?
french: Qu'est-ce que tu lis ?
russian: Ты что, читаешь там?
bulgarian: What are you reading?

english: Oh March, you're so funny!
french: Oh March, tu es trop drôle !
russian: О, Март, ты такой смешной!
bulgarian: Oh March, you're so funny!

english: Time for bed. That's your cue to leave.
french: Je vais dormir. Sous-entendu, tu t'en vas ?
russian: Пора спать. Это твой сигнал на выход.
bulgarian: Time for bed. That's your cue to leave.

english: Take notes, [Ari]...my swing is poetry in motion.
french: Observe bien, [Ari]... Ce mouvement de marteau, c'est de la poésie pure.
russian: Запоминай, [Ari]... мои удары — чистая поэзия в движении.
bulgarian: Take notes, [Ari]...my swing is poetry in motion.

english: The name's March... What do you want?
french: Moi, c'est March... Tu me veux quoi ?
russian: Я Март... Чего надо?
bulgarian: The name's March... What do you want?

english: I'm [Ari], the new farmer in town!
french: Moi, c'est [Ari]. Je viens de reprendre la ferme !
russian:
Я [Ari],

новые фермер

новая фермеркановый фермерновое фермер в городе!
bulgarian: I'm [Ari], the new farmer in town!

english: Charming.
french: Sympa...
russian: Очаровательно.
bulgarian: Charming.

english: I don't see what that has to do with me.
french: Qu'est-ce que tu veux que ça me fasse ?
russian: И какое мне до этого должно быть дело? Не важно, что там Аделина говорит, нам в городе не нужны чужаки, чтобы решить наши проблемы.
bulgarian: I don't see what that has to do with me.

english: Regardless of what Adeline says, we really don't need an outsider to come in and solve our problems for us.
french: Malgré ce que dit Adeline, on n'a pas besoin d'étrangers pour régler nos problèmes à notre place.
russian:
Ты, должно быть,

те самые «фермер», о которых

та самая «фермерка», о которойтот самый «фермер», о которомто самое «фермер», о которых тут все говорят. Не важно, что там говорит Аделина. Нам не нужны чужаки, чтобы решить наши проблемы.
bulgarian: Regardless of what Adeline says, we really don't need an outsider to come in and solve our problems for us.

english: You must be this "farmer" folks are talking about.
french: C'est sûrement de toi que tout le monde parle en ce moment.
russian: Я- То есть мы прекрасно справляемся сами. Просто не мешай.
bulgarian: You must be this "farmer" folks are talking about.

english: Regardless of what Adeline says, we don't need an outsider to come in and solve our problems for us.
french: Malgré ce que dit Adeline, on n'a pas besoin d'étrangers pour régler nos problèmes à notre place.
bulgarian: Regardless of what Adeline says, we don't need an outsider to come in and solve our problems for us.

english: I- We have everything under control. Just don't get in the way.
french: Je... enfin, on gère la situation. Évite de te fourrer dans nos pattes.
bulgarian: I- We have everything under control. Just don't get in the way.

english: It might be time to upgrade my hammer... don't get too excited, [Ari]. I don't do hand-me-downs.
french: Je vais devoir investir dans un nouveau marteau... Je te vois venir, [Ari]. Je ne te donnerai pas l'ancien.
russian: Пожалуй, пора сменить молот... не радуйся раньше времени, [Ari]. Я свои инструменты не раздаю.
bulgarian: It might be time to upgrade my hammer... don't get too excited, [Ari]. I don't do hand-me-downs.

english: He's probably eating a $Hard Boiled Egg$ right now.
french: D'ailleurs il est sûrement en train d'en manger un en ce moment même.
russian: Скорее всего, он прямо сейчас ест $варёное яйцо$.
bulgarian: He's probably eating a $Hard Boiled Egg$ right now.

english: If it wasn't for me, Olric wouldn't eat any vegetables. He'd have $Hard Boiled Eggs$ for every meal!
french: Si je n'étais pas là, Olric ne mangerait jamais de légumes. Ce serait $œufs durs$ à chaque repas !
russian: Если бы не я, Ольрик вообще бы овощей не ел. Ел бы только $варёные яйца$ на завтрак, обед и ужин!
bulgarian: If it wasn't for me, Olric wouldn't eat any vegetables. He'd have $Hard Boiled Eggs$ for every meal!

english: What?
french: Qu'est-ce qu'il y a ?
russian: Что?
bulgarian: What?

english: Why are you looking at me like that...?
french: Pourquoi tu me regardes comme ça...?
russian: Чего ты так смотришь?..
bulgarian: Why are you looking at me like that...?

english: Hey, [Ari]. How's it going?
french: Salut, [Ari]. Comment ça va ?
russian: Привет, [Ari]. Как дела?
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]. How's it going?

english: What do you want? Make it quick.
french: Qu'est-ce que tu veux ? Va droit au but.
russian: Что нужно? Говори быстрее.
bulgarian: What do you want? Make it quick.

english: And I don't know what Adeline was thinking, giving it away to some stranger.
french: Et je ne sais pas non plus quelle mouche a piqué Adeline en la donnant à quelqu'un d'extérieur au village.
russian: И что Аделина вообще думала, отдавая её кому попало?
bulgarian: And I don't know what Adeline was thinking, giving it away to some stranger.

english: I don't know what you're hoping to gain by taking over that farm.
french: Je ne vois pas l'intérêt de s'occuper de cette vieille ferme.
russian: Не понимаю, что ты надеешься получить, взявшись за ту ферму.
bulgarian: I don't know what you're hoping to gain by taking over that farm.

english: This is a big, important order. So unless this is a big, important conversation...
french: J'ai une grosse commande à honorer, alors si tu n'as rien d'important à me dire...
russian: У меня тут важный заказ. Так что, если это не важный разговор...
bulgarian: This is a big, important order. So unless this is a big, important conversation...

english: In the zone.
french: Ah oui ! À fond.
russian: В потоке.
bulgarian: In the zone.

english: I'm really... what is it Olric's always saying?
french: Je suis... C'est quoi l'expression d'Olric, déjà ?
russian: Я прямо сейчас... как там говорит Ольрик?
bulgarian: I'm really... what is it Olric's always saying?

english: Maybe I can make some kind of sharpener people can use at home...
french: Il faudrait que j'invente un outil pour affûter ses couteaux chez soi...
russian: Может, сделать точилку, чтобы люди могли пользоваться дома...
bulgarian: Maybe I can make some kind of sharpener people can use at home...

english: I didn't realize there'd be such a demand for knife sharpening.
french: Je n'imaginais pas avoir autant de demandes pour affûter des couteaux.
russian: Не думал, что заточка ножей будет настолько востребована.
bulgarian: I didn't realize there'd be such a demand for knife sharpening.

english: Landen brags a lot, but he really knows his stuff.
french: Landen n'est pas très modeste, mais ça se comprend.
russian: Ланден много хвастается, но в деле он разбирается.
bulgarian: Landen brags a lot, but he really knows his stuff.

english: Are you going to take a bath? Fine, I was leaving anyway.
french: Tu viens prendre un bain ? Ça tombe bien. J'allais partir.
russian: Ты собираешься в ванну? Ладно, я как раз уходил.
bulgarian: Are you going to take a bath? Fine, I was leaving anyway.

english: I know I make it look easy, but that's from long practice.
french: Je sais que ça a l'air facile quand on me voit faire, mais j'ai beaucoup travaillé pour en arriver là.
russian: Знаю, выглядит легко, но это — результат многолетней практики.
bulgarian: I know I make it look easy, but that's from long practice.

english: We're lucky to have Balor here, his prices are fairer than other merchants that have come through Mistria.
french: On a de la chance d'avoir Balor, ses prix sont plus raisonnables que beaucoup d'autres marchands qui sont passés par Mistria.
russian: Нам повезло, что Балор здесь. Цены у него честнее, чем у других торговцев, что бывали в Мистрии.
bulgarian: We're lucky to have Balor here, his prices are fairer than other merchants that have come through Mistria.

english: An order for anything but nails makes my day.
french: Quand on me commande autre chose que des clous, je suis heureux.
russian: Заказ на что угодно, кроме гвоздей, поднимает мне настроение.
bulgarian: An order for anything but nails makes my day.

english: Valen asked me to make medical instruments.
french: Valen m'a demandé de lui fabriquer des instruments chirurgicaux.
russian: Вален попросила меня сделать медицинские инструменты.
bulgarian: Valen asked me to make medical instruments.

english: Balor said his wagon took some, uh, battle damage. What is he doing with it, anyway? Off-roading?
french: Balor m'a dit qu'il avait abîmé son chariot pendant sa tournée. Mais il fait où avec ?
russian: Балор сказал, его фургон получил, эээ, боевые повреждения. Он его, что, по скалам гоняет?
bulgarian: Balor said his wagon took some, uh, battle damage. What is he doing with it, anyway? Off-roading?

english: A messy forge can be dangerous, so I take cleaning seriously.
french: Une forge en désordre, c'est synonyme de danger, alors je m'efforce de tout ranger correctement.
russian: Кузня в беспорядке — опасное место, так что я к уборке отношусь серьёзно.
bulgarian: A messy forge can be dangerous, so I take cleaning seriously.

english: When the mine was open, I never had to worry about supplies. I've had to learn how to do a lot with a little.
french: Quand la mine était encore en activité, je ne m'inquiétais pas de l'approvisionnement en matières premières. Depuis, je fais attention à ce que j'utilise.
russian: Когда шахта была открыта, за недостаток материалов переживать не приходилось. Теперь пришлось научиться делать многое из малого.
bulgarian: When the mine was open, I never had to worry about supplies. I've had to learn how to do a lot with a little.

english: At least I can still look forward to the Inn placing orders for new knives.
french: Au moins, je reçois régulièrement des commandes de couteaux pour l'auberge.
russian: Хотя бы трактир продолжает заказывать у меня новые ножи.
bulgarian: At least I can still look forward to the Inn placing orders for new knives.

english: I miss making swords. It's just too big of a material waste.
french: Forger des épées me manque, mais je ne peux pas me permettre de gaspiller autant de ressources.
russian: Скучаю по изготовлению мечей. Но там слишком много материала уходит впустую.
bulgarian: I miss making swords. It's just too big of a material waste.

english: Oh, is it raining? I barely noticed.
french: Oh, il pleut ? Je n'avais même pas remarqué.
russian: А, дождь? Даже не заметил.
bulgarian: Oh, is it raining? I barely noticed.

english: We get most of our meals at the Inn these days. Olric trying to fry eggs on the forge was stressing me out...
french: On prend la plupart de nos repas à l'auberge, ces temps-ci. Ça me stressait de voir Olric se faire des œufs au plat dans ma forge...
russian: Сейчас мы почти всегда едим в трактире. Когда Ольрик пытался жарить яйца в горне, я чуть с ума не сошёл...
bulgarian: We get most of our meals at the Inn these days. Olric trying to fry eggs on the forge was stressing me out...

english: Some of it's obvious, but some of it... man. Impressive.
french: Pour certains, c'est évident, mais pour d'autres... waouh, c'est impressionnant.
russian: Что-то очевидно, но что-то... ух. Впечатляет.
bulgarian: Some of it's obvious, but some of it... man. Impressive.

english: I'm always trying to work out how old metalwork was done.
french: J'essaie toujours de comprendre comment on forgeait des outils autrefois.
russian: Я всё время пытаюсь понять, как делали металл в старину.
bulgarian: I'm always trying to work out how old metalwork was done.

english: Whew, I need a break. Can't rush perfection.
french: Pfiou, j'ai besoin d'une pause. On n'atteint pas la perfection dans la précipitation.
russian: Фух, мне нужен перерыв. Совершенство не любит спешки.
bulgarian: Whew, I need a break. Can't rush perfection.

english: You need something? Otherwise I'm working.
french: Tu as besoin de quelque chose ? Parce que je travaille, là.
russian: Тебе что-то нужно? Иначе я занят.
bulgarian: You need something? Otherwise I'm working.

english: This new piece is going to turn heads. I'm hoping Balor takes an interest and finds a buyer in the Capital.
french: Cette nouvelle pièce va en impressionner plus d'un. J'espère qu'elle intéressera Balor et qu'il trouvera un acheteur à la capitale.
russian: Эта новая работа точно привлечёт внимание. Надеюсь, Балор заинтересуется и найдёт покупателя в столице.
bulgarian: This new piece is going to turn heads. I'm hoping Balor takes an interest and finds a buyer in the Capital.

english: Josephine asked me to make new silverware for the Inn, and she kept it simple, but... I've got ideas...
french: Joséphine veut changer les couverts de l'auberge... Elle veut quelque chose de sobre, mais j'ai quelques idées en plus...
russian: Джозефина заказала новые столовые приборы для трактира. Хотела простенько... но у меня уже идеи...
bulgarian: Josephine asked me to make new silverware for the Inn, and she kept it simple, but... I've got ideas...

english: Olric always asks me to work out with him, but working at the forge is enough for me.
french: Olric veut toujours que je m'entraîne avec lui, mais je fais suffisamment d'exercice à la forge.
russian: Ольрик всё зовёт меня потренироваться, но кузница — это и так тренировка.
bulgarian: Olric always asks me to work out with him, but working at the forge is enough for me.

english: I heard Olric is at the woodshop... is he getting into trouble with the old-timers again?
french: Il paraît qu'Olric est à l'atelier de menuiserie... Il a encore des ennuis avec les petits vieux ?
russian: Слышал, Ольрик в столярной... Опять с ветеранами там зацепился?
bulgarian: I heard Olric is at the woodshop... is he getting into trouble with the old-timers again?

english: If you want to thank Olric for always being so nice to you, he always appreciates a nice piece of $Stone$. He likes to collect them.
french: Si tu cherches un moyen de remercier Olric, tu peux lui offrir une $pierre$. Il en fait collection.
russian: Если хочешь отблагодарить Ольрика за доброту — он обожает хорошие куски $камня$. Коллекционирует.
bulgarian: If you want to thank Olric for always being so nice to you, he always appreciates a nice piece of $Stone$. He likes to collect them.

english: Hm... I'm starting to run low on ore. Better talk to Adeline about getting another request on the board soon...
french: Mmm... Je commence à être à court de minerai. Je vais voir avec Adeline si je peux publier une nouvelle requête...
russian: Хм... руда заканчивается. Надо поговорить с Аделиной, чтобы повесить новый заказ.
bulgarian: Hm... I'm starting to run low on ore. Better talk to Adeline about getting another request on the board soon...

english: I've got places to be, [Ari]. I bet you do too, so let's keep it moving.
french: J'ai plein de choses à faire, [Ari]. Toi aussi sûrement, alors ne perdons pas notre temps.
russian: У меня свои дела, [Ari]. Уверен, у тебя тоже — так что давай побыстрее.
bulgarian: I've got places to be, [Ari]. I bet you do too, so let's keep it moving.

english: I'm never satisfied with the day if I haven't spent some time at the forge.
french: Si je ne passe pas un peu de temps à la forge, j'ai l'impression d'avoir perdu ma journée.
russian: Если не провожу хотя бы часть дня в кузне, кажется, что ничего не сделал.
bulgarian: I'm never satisfied with the day if I haven't spent some time at the forge.

english: We've had a problem getting enough ore ever since the Earthquake shut down the Mines.
french: J'ai du mal à me procurer de minerai depuis la fermeture des mines, suite au tremblement de terre.
russian: С рудой беда с тех пор, как землетрясение накрыло шахты.
bulgarian: We've had a problem getting enough ore ever since the Earthquake shut down the Mines.

english: As much as I enjoy it when you stop to talk, do you have to do it in the rain?
french: J'aime bien discuter le bout de gras, mais on est obligés de le faire sous la pluie ?
russian: Мне, конечно, приятно, когда ты подходишь поболтать, но обязательно под дождём?
bulgarian: As much as I enjoy it when you stop to talk, do you have to do it in the rain?

english: The forge gets nice and cool on rainy days.
french: La forge reste bien fraîche les jours de pluie.
russian: В дождь в кузнице приятно, прохладно.
bulgarian: The forge gets nice and cool on rainy days.

english: Olric says there's plenty to do indoors on a rainy day, but it's not forgework.
french: D'après Olric, on peut faire plein de choses à l'intérieur quand il pleut. Plein de choses, sauf travailler le métal...
russian: Ольрик говорит, что в дождь и в доме дел полно, но это не то же самое, что работать в кузне.
bulgarian: Olric says there's plenty to do indoors on a rainy day, but it's not forgework.

english: Can't let a little rain slow me down.
french: Je ne vais pas laisser un peu de pluie me ralentir.
russian: Мелкий дождик меня не остановит.
bulgarian: Can't let a little rain slow me down.

english: I keep the forge hot, even on rainy days.
french: Même quand il pleut, j'arrive à maintenir la forge à température.
russian: Я держу горн горячим даже в дождь.
bulgarian: I keep the forge hot, even on rainy days.

english: You need our gear? Makes sense.
french: Tu as besoin de notre matériel ? Ça n'a rien d'étonnant.
russian: Нужна наша экипировка? Логично.
bulgarian: You need our gear? Makes sense.

english: Oh, it's you. Well if you need something...
french: Oh, c'est toi. Si tu as besoin de quelque chose, fais-moi signe...
russian: А, это ты. Ну, если что нужно...
bulgarian: Oh, it's you. Well if you need something...

english: You can just leave your money by the till, you know.
french: Tu peux laisser les sous à côté de la caisse, tu sais.
russian: Можешь просто оставить деньги у кассы, если что.
bulgarian: You can just leave your money by the till, you know.

english: Doing some shopping?
french: Tu es là pour acheter ?
russian: Закупаешься?
bulgarian: Doing some shopping?

english: Let me know if you need anything, [Ari].
french: N'hésite pas si tu as besoin de quelque chose, [Ari].
russian: Скажи, если что-то нужно, [Ari].

french: En ville, les couleurs automnales sont très jolies, mais ici, à la ferme, elles sont époustouflantes.
russian: Город в осенних цветах выглядит красиво, но это ничто по сравнению с твоей фермой.
bulgarian: Fall colors in town look great, but they look even more amazing here on the farm.

english: The trees aren't even that close! How are leaves getting over to the forge?
french: Il n'y a même pas d'arbres tout près ! Comment elles font pour arriver jusqu'à la forge ?
russian: Деревья там даже не близко! Как эти листья умудряются падать в кузницу?
bulgarian: The trees aren't even that close! How are leaves getting over to the forge?

english: Can trees mess with you? Should we ask Celine!?
french: Les arbres peuvent nous embêter exprès ? On devrait poser la question à Céline, tu crois ?!
russian: Деревья умеют нарочно дразниться? Может, нам спросить Селин?!
bulgarian: Can trees mess with you? Should we ask Celine!?

english: I'm always sweeping leaves around the anvil in fall...
french: En automne, je n'arrête pas de balayer les feuilles autour de l'enclume...
russian: Осенью я вечно сметаю листву от наковальни...
bulgarian: I'm always sweeping leaves around the anvil in fall...

english: And I've been thinking... it's just us out here, right?
french: Et je me disais... il n'y a que toi et moi, ici, n'est-ce pas ?
russian: И я подумал... Тут ведь кроме нас никого нет?
bulgarian: And I've been thinking... it's just us out here, right?

english: So maybe if I sweep up the leaves while you're out, we can do it later. If you want.
french: Peut-être que si je balaie les feuilles pour en faire un tas pendant que tu es dehors, on pourra sauter dedans plus tard. Si tu en as envie.
russian: Может, я смету листья, пока тебя нет, а потом попробуем прыгнуть. Если хочешь.
bulgarian: So maybe if I sweep up the leaves while you're out, we can do it later. If you want.

english: Olric and I used to go diving into leaf piles when we were kids.
french: Quand on était gamins, Olric et moi, on sautait dans les tas de feuilles.
russian: В детстве мы с Ольриком часто ныряли в кучи листьев.
bulgarian: Olric and I used to go diving into leaf piles when we were kids.

english: I was thinking about this when I woke up, but... I sleep a lot better next to you, you know that?
french: Je me suis fait une réflexion ce matin, en me levant... Je dors bien mieux avec toi à mes côtés, tu sais.
russian: Когда я проснулся, мне пришло в голову... Ты знаешь, что с тобой мне спится гораздо лучше?
bulgarian: I was thinking about this when I woke up, but... I sleep a lot better next to you, you know that?

english: You sleep okay?
french: Tu euh... tu as bien dormi ?
russian: Как, эм... Как тебе спалось?
bulgarian: You sleep okay?

english: Morning, [Ari].
french: Bonjour, [Ari].
russian: Утро, [Ari].
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari].

english: Did you get soaked working all day out there? Want me to warm you up?
french: Tu as travaillé à l'extérieur toute la journée, tu as dû te faire tremper. Tu veux que je te réchauffe ?
russian:
Ты наверняка

промокли

промоклапромокпромокло за работой. Хочешь, я тебя согрею?
bulgarian: Did you get soaked working all day out there? Want me to warm you up?

english: It's been really coming down all day, huh...
french: Il n'a pas cessé de pleuvoir, aujourd'hui, hein...
russian: Хм, весь день льёт как из ведра...
bulgarian: It's been really coming down all day, huh...

english: Heh. Me, either. No wonder we're married.
french: Ha. Moi, c'est pareil. Pas étonnant qu'on soit mariés.
russian: Хех. Вот и я нет. Понятно, почему мы с тобой супруги.
bulgarian: Heh. Me, either. No wonder we're married.

english: Do you ever take the day off when it's raining?
french: Est-ce que tu prends parfois un jour de congé, quand il pleut ?
russian: Ты хоть иногда устраиваешь себе выходной из-за дождя?
bulgarian: Do you ever take the day off when it's raining?

english: I wouldn't have minded a late morning lying around in bed with you...
french: Je n'aurais pas dit non à une grasse matinée au lit avec toi...
russian: Я бы не отказался этим утром поваляться подольше в кровати вдвоём...
bulgarian: I wouldn't have minded a late morning lying around in bed with you...

english: There's still time, you know.
french: On a encore le temps, tu sais.
russian: Ещё не поздно вернуться.
bulgarian: There's still time, you know.

english: Ugh, I can't stop yawning.
french: Ah, je n'arrive pas à m'arrêter de bâiller.
russian: Гх, никак не перестану зевать.
bulgarian: Ugh, I can't stop yawning.

english: It's so pristine I don't want to touch it...
french: Elle est si immaculée que je n'ose pas la toucher...
russian: Такой чистый, что даже не хочется трогать.
bulgarian: It's so pristine I don't want to touch it...

english: On the other hand, it makes me want to build a big double-decker snow house with you.
french: Et en même temps, ça me donne envie de construire une énorme maison en neige à deux niveaux avec toi.
russian: А с другой стороны, из него хочется построить огромный двухэтажный дом. Вместе с тобой.
bulgarian: On the other hand, it makes me want to build a big double-decker snow house with you.

english: The snow looks so pretty out here on the farm.
french: La neige est tellement jolie ici, sur la ferme.
russian: У тебя на ферме снег такой красивый.
bulgarian: The snow looks so pretty out here on the farm.

english: I might go out, too. I like studying how icicles freeze along the edge of the roof... sometimes it looks like filigree.
french: Je vais peut-être faire un tour dehors, moi aussi. J'aime regarder comment les stalactites se forment le long du toit... On dirait parfois un filigrane.
russian: Может, я тоже выйду. Люблю рассматривать, как сосульки замерзают на крыше... Иногда выглядит совершенно филигранно.
bulgarian: I might go out, too. I like studying how icicles freeze along the edge of the roof... sometimes it looks like filigree.

english: Are you heading out today? Bundle up.
french: Tu sors, aujourd'hui ? Couvre-toi bien.
russian: Ты сегодня на улицу? Укутайся хорошенько.
bulgarian: Are you heading out today? Bundle up.

english: And I got pretty into the details on a piece for a client in the Capital.
french: Sans compter que je me suis lancé dans un travail assez minutieux sur une pièce destinée à un client de la capitale.
russian: И мне надо доделать мелочи по одной тонкой работе для столичного клиента.
bulgarian: And I got pretty into the details on a piece for a client in the Capital.

english: Also want to check in on Olric. He's pretty self-sufficient, but sometimes he stays up all night looking at his rock collection...
french: Je voudrais aussi aller voir si Olric va bien. Il peut se débrouiller seul, mais parfois, il passe la nuit entière à admirer sa collection de cailloux...
russian: А ещё хочу проведать Ольрика. Он довольно самостоятельный, но иногда всю ночь рассматривает свою коллекцию камней вместо тог, чтобы спать.
bulgarian: Also want to check in on Olric. He's pretty self-sufficient, but sometimes he stays up all night looking at his rock collection...

english: Think I'll head over to the forge today. There's some last minute orders from Adeline...
french: Je crois que je vais aller faire un tour à la forge, aujourd'hui. Adeline m'a passé quelques commandes de dernière minute...
russian: Думаю, я сегодня пойду в кузницу. Пришли срочные заказы от Аделины...
bulgarian: Think I'll head over to the forge today. There's some last minute orders from Adeline...

english: I don't like the idea of tracking dirt all over our cute house.
french: Je n'aime pas l'idée de laisser des traces de terre partout dans notre jolie maison.
russian: Не хочу развозить грязь по нашему симпатичному дому.
bulgarian: I don't like the idea of tracking dirt all over our cute house.

english: Ugh, the roads get so muddy in spring...
french: Pfff, les chemins sont tellement boueux, au printemps...
russian: Гх, весной дороги превращаются в слякоть.
bulgarian: Ugh, the roads get so muddy in spring...

english: It's a nice change from the smell of charcoal.
french: Ça change agréablement de l'odeur du charbon.
russian: Приятное разнообразие после запаха угольной гари.
bulgarian: It's a nice change from the smell of charcoal.

english: The spring breeze smells so nice on the farm... it's so earthy.
french: La brise de printemps sent tellement bon, sur la ferme... Elle a une odeur de terre.
russian: Весенний ветерок разносит по ферме такой приятный аромат... очень землистый.
bulgarian: The spring breeze smells so nice on the farm... it's so earthy.

english: Do you think Valen's got an allergy syrup or something?
french: Tu crois que Valen aurait un sirop contre les allergies, ou quelque chose comme ça ?
russian: Как ты думаешь, у Вален есть сироп от аллергии?
bulgarian: Do you think Valen's got an allergy syrup or something?

english: Maybe I'll swing by the Clinic... ugh...
french: Je vais peut-être passer à la clinique... argh...
russian: Может, зайти к ней в клинику... ох...
bulgarian: Maybe I'll swing by the Clinic... ugh...

english: Hey, are my eyes red? My allergies are going crazy.
french: Dis, est-ce que j'ai les yeux rouges ? Mes allergies se déchaînent.
russian: Слушай, у меня глаза красные? Аллергия просто замучила.
bulgarian: Hey, are my eyes red? My allergies are going crazy.

english: So if you need an extra pair of hands around the farm, just say the word.
french: Si tu as besoin d'une paire de bras supplémentaires à la ferme, tu n'as qu'un mot à dire.
russian: Так что если понадобится помощь по ферме, только скажи.
bulgarian: So if you need an extra pair of hands around the farm, just say the word.

english: I always get so much energy in the spring.
french: Je me sens toujours plein d'énergie, au printemps.
russian: Весной я всегда полон энергии.
bulgarian: I always get so much energy in the spring.

english: Is it too hot to cuddle in bed? We should try anyway.
french: Tu crois qu'il fait trop chaud pour rester au lit ? On devrait au moins essayer.
russian: Слишком жарко, чтобы обниматься в постели, да? Ничего, всё равно попробуем.
bulgarian: Is it too hot to cuddle in bed? We should try anyway.

english: Ugh, this heat...
french: Argh, quelle chaleur...
russian: Ох, ну и жарища...
bulgarian: Ugh, this heat...

english: It's nice to fall asleep together with a cool breeze, right?
french: C'est agréable de s'endormir ensemble sous une brise fraîche, non ?
russian: Приятно засыпать вдвоём под прохладный ветерок, да ведь?
bulgarian: It's nice to fall asleep together with a cool breeze, right?

english: I love keeping the windows open in summer...
french: J'adore laisser les fenêtres ouvertes en été...
russian: Обожаю летом держать окна настежь...
bulgarian: I love keeping the windows open in summer...

english: I'm usually pretty good at keeping the forge fire steady just by feeling the heat...
french: Habituellement, j'arrive à maintenir le feu de la forge à une température stable, rien qu'en sentant sa chaleur...
russian: Обычно я неплохо поддерживаю огонь в печи, полагаясь на свои ощущения...
bulgarian: I'm usually pretty good at keeping the forge fire steady just by feeling the heat...

english: Except in this season. It's already hot, so it trips me up!
french: Sauf en cette saison. Il fait déjà chaud, alors ça me déboussole !
russian: Но не в этот сезон. Вокруг всегда жара, так что я чувства меня обманывают!
bulgarian: Except in this season. It's already hot, so it trips me up!

english: The beginning of summer always throws me off my game.
french: Le début de l'été me perturbe toujours.
russian: В начале лета у меня всегда притупляется чутьё.
bulgarian: The beginning of summer always throws me off my game.

english: I used to spend every day working, but now I want to take more time off and spend it with you.
french: Autrefois, je travaillais tous les jours, mais maintenant, j'ai envie de prendre du temps libre et de le passer avec toi.
russian: Раньше я каждый день проводил за работой. А теперь мне чаще хочется брать выходные, чтобы быть рядом с тобой.
bulgarian: I used to spend every day working, but now I want to take more time off and spend it with you.

english: Hey, let's go to the Beach soon!
french: D'ailleurs, il faudrait qu'on aille à la plage, un de ces quatre !
russian: Слушай, а давай выберемся на пляж!
bulgarian: Hey, let's go to the Beach soon!

english: Spending summer with you is... pretty great.
french: Passer l'été avec toi, c'est... plutôt génial.
russian: Проводить лето вместе с тобой... очень приятно.
bulgarian: Spending summer with you is... pretty great.

english: Come on, let's get into bed. I'll warm you up.
french: Viens, mettons-nous au lit. Je te réchaufferai.
russian: Пойдём, пора в кровать. Я тебя согрею.
bulgarian: Come on, let's get into bed. I'll warm you up.

english: The night got cold really fast, didn't it?
french: Les nuits se sont rafraîchies très rapidement, tu ne trouves pas ?
russian: Ночью так резко похолодало!
bulgarian: The night got cold really fast, didn't it?

english: When the sky's clear, we should go up to the summit together.
french: Quand le ciel est dégagé, on devrait grimper jusqu'au sommet, tous les deux.
russian: Нам надо вместе сходить на вершину, когда будет ясное небо.
bulgarian: When the sky's clear, we should go up to the summit together.

english: Winter's a really nice time for stargazing...
french: L'hiver est vraiment une belle période pour admirer les étoiles...
russian: Зима — хорошее время, чтобы посмотреть на звёзды...
bulgarian: Winter's a really nice time for stargazing...

english: Then they look over my shoulder and say whatever they want...
french: Ils regardent par-dessus mon épaule et font des commentaires...
russian: А потом ещё заглядывают мне под руку и мелют всякую чепуху...
bulgarian: Then they look over my shoulder and say whatever they want...

english: Well... I guess I don't mind the company, so it's alright.
french: Enfin... Ça ne me gêne pas d'avoir de la compagnie, alors ce n'est pas grave.
russian: Впрочем... Не беда, я не против их общества.
bulgarian: Well... I guess I don't mind the company, so it's alright.

english: Winter means the freeloaders hang around the forge to warm themselves up.
french: En hiver, il y a toujours des profiteurs qui traînent autour de la forge pour se réchauffer.
russian: Зимой всякие бездельники собираются у печи погреться.
bulgarian: Winter means the freeloaders hang around the forge to warm themselves up.

english: I'm glad I can share it with you.
french: Je suis heureux de pouvoir en profiter avec toi.
russian: Я рад, что могу разделить его с тобой.
bulgarian: I'm glad I can share it with you.

english: The view out here on the farm is beautiful in winter, [Ari].
french: La vue qu'on a sur la ferme est magnifique en hiver, [Ari].
russian: На твоей ферме зимой открывается потрясающий вид, [Ari].
bulgarian: The view out here on the farm is beautiful in winter, [Ari].

english: I'll be back with you soon, okay?
french: Je te rejoins très vite, d'accord ?
russian: Скоро вернусь и поболтаем, хорошо?
bulgarian: I'll be back with you soon, okay?

english: Oh! Sorry, [Ari], I was totally in the zone with work...
french: Oh ! Désolé, [Ari], j'étais totalement concentré sur mon travail...
russian: Ой! Прости, [Ari], я так увлёкся работой...
bulgarian: Oh! Sorry, [Ari], I was totally in the zone with work...

english: So when you're making an alloy, you have to be mindful of how the metals change each other.
french: Alors quand on fabrique un alliage, il faut être très attentif à la façon dont ils s'influencent.
russian: Так что когда изготавливаешь сплав, надо следить, как металлы взаимодействуют друг с другом.
bulgarian: So when you're making an alloy, you have to be mindful of how the metals change each other.

english: I guess people are like that, too...
french: C'est comme dans la vraie vie...
russian: Впрочем, в жизни тоже так...
bulgarian: I guess people are like that, too...

english: Iron, Silver, Gold... they all have different attributes.
french: Fer, argent, or... Chaque métal a des propriétés et une température de fonte différentes.
russian: Железо, серебро, золото... У всех металлов разные свойства и разные точки плавления.
bulgarian: Iron, Silver, Gold... they all have different attributes.

english: If the whole thing's going to be ornamental, then maybe I should cast it instead of forging it...
french: Si c'est destiné à être purement décoratif, je devrais peut-être le mouler, plutôt que le forger...
russian: Если это такая орнаментальная композиция, может, лучше её не ковать, а отлить...
bulgarian: If the whole thing's going to be ornamental, then maybe I should cast it instead of forging it...

english: How should I tackle this project...
french: Comment je vais gérer ce projet...?
russian: Как бы подступиться к этому проекту...
bulgarian: How should I tackle this project...

english: Ugh, I can't fall asleep now! I have work to do!
french: Argh, je ne dois pas m'endormir maintenant ! J'ai du travail !
russian: Гх, я теперь не могу заснуть! У меня ещё работа!
bulgarian: Ugh, I can't fall asleep now! I have work to do!

english: I was just going to sit down for a second but then I got real tired...
french: Je voulais juste m'asseoir une seconde, et puis j'ai eu un gros coup de fatigue...
russian: Я хотел просто на секундочку присесть, но вдруг почувствовал такую усталость...
bulgarian: I was just going to sit down for a second but then I got real tired...

english: It's not a bad book or anything but there's a lot of, um...
french: Il n'est pas mauvais, simplement, il y a beaucoup de... hum...
russian: Неплохая в общем-то книга, но там очень много, эм...
bulgarian: It's not a bad book or anything but there's a lot of, um...

english: Nevermind! I'm going to keep reading!
french: Peu importe ! Je vais continuer à le lire !
russian: Не важно! Пойду дальше читать!
bulgarian: Nevermind! I'm going to keep reading!

english: Elsie insisted I borrow this book from her.
french: Elsie a insisté pour que je lui emprunte ce livre.
russian: Элси настоятельно рекомендовала мне одолжить у неё эту книгу.
bulgarian: Elsie insisted I borrow this book from her.

english: But I'm actually thinking deeply about my craft.
french: Mais en réalité, je suis en pleine réflexion sur mon art.
russian: Но вообще-то я погружён в размышления о кузнечном деле.
bulgarian: But I'm actually thinking deeply about my craft.

english: As you're aware, this is an important part of being an artisan.
french: Comme tu le sais, c'est une part importante du métier d'artisan.
russian: Как тебе известно, для всякого ремесленника это важная часть работы.
bulgarian: As you're aware, this is an important part of being an artisan.

english: Also, please wake me up if I fall asleep.
french: D'ailleurs, réveille-moi si tu vois que je m'endors, s'il te plaît.
russian: И всё-таки, разбуди меня, пожалуйста, если засну.
bulgarian: Also, please wake me up if I fall asleep.

english: I might look like I'm relaxing...
french: Je donne peut-être l'impression d'être en train de me détendre...
russian: Со стороны может показаться, что я прохлаждаюсь...
bulgarian: I might look like I'm relaxing...

english: Iron burns bright orange, though.
french: Celle du fer, en revanche, est orange vif.
russian: А вот железо даёт ярко-рыжий.
bulgarian: Iron burns bright orange, though.

english: I'll show you some time.
french: Je te montrerai, à l'occasion.
russian: Я тебе как-нибудь покажу.
bulgarian: I'll show you some time.

english: Did you know that copper burns green?
french: Tu savais que lorsqu'on brûlait du cuivre, sa flamme était verte ?
russian: Ты знаешь, что медь горит зелёным пламенем?
bulgarian: Did you know that copper burns green?

english: Most smiths would kill for a patron like Eiland, you know.
french: Tu sais, la plupart des forgerons tueraient pour avoir un mécène comme Eiland.
russian: Такого покровителя как Эйланд большинство кузнецов видели только в мечтах.
bulgarian: Most smiths would kill for a patron like Eiland, you know.

english: It's nice living in town with an eccentric noble who's obsessed with commissioning reproductions.
french: C'est sympa de vivre dans une ville occupée par un noble excentrique qui ne pense qu'à commander des reproductions.
russian: Удобно жить в городе с эксцентричным дворянином, помешанным на репродукциях.
bulgarian: It's nice living in town with an eccentric noble who's obsessed with commissioning reproductions.

english: Looks like March's star is rising!
french: On dirait que March devient l'étoile montante !
russian: Кажется, звезда Марта начинает восход!
bulgarian: Looks like March's star is rising!

english: I've been getting more and more custom orders from the Capital lately.
french: Depuis quelque temps, j'ai de plus en plus de commandes venant de la capitale.
russian: В последнее время у меня всё больше индивидуальных заказов из столицы.
bulgarian: I've been getting more and more custom orders from the Capital lately.

english: I think our animals will do well this year.
bulgarian: I think our animals will do well this year.

english: Even if we don't bring home any ribbons, I know they're all winners.
bulgarian: Even if we don't bring home any ribbons, I know they're all winners.

english: Happy $Animal Festival$!
bulgarian: Happy $Animal Festival$!

english: I know everyone's excited over the big harvest feast this year...
bulgarian: I know everyone's excited over the big harvest feast this year...

english: But I'm honestly looking forward to a dance with you.
bulgarian: But I'm honestly looking forward to a dance with you.

english: Morning, [Ari]... Happy $Harvest Festival$!
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]... Happy $Harvest Festival$!

english: If you'd like to see them up on the summit... I'd like that, too.
bulgarian: If you'd like to see them up on the summit... I'd like that, too.

english: Hey, [Ari]... it's the $Shooting Star Festival$ tonight.
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]... it's the $Shooting Star Festival$ tonight.

english: I've been seeing you collect $Breath of Spring$ all over the farm...
bulgarian: I've been seeing you collect $Breath of Spring$ all over the farm...

russian: Пора мне вернуться к работе.
bulgarian: I should get back to work.

english: You should come by the forge whenever you want.
french: Tu peux passer à la forge quand tu veux.
russian: Приходи в кузницу, когда тебе захочется.
bulgarian: You should come by the forge whenever you want.

english: Said he'd been starting to wonder if there might be something between you and me.
french: Il m'a demandé s'il n'y avait pas quelque chose entre toi et moi.
russian: Он сказал, любопытно, что у нас с тобой происходит.
bulgarian: Said he'd been starting to wonder if there might be something between you and me.

english: Because a pair of blacksmiths like us were 'bound to make sparks fly.'
french: Parce qu'un forgeron en couple, ça « ferait des étincelles ».
russian: Потому что «меж двух кузнецов искры летят».
bulgarian: Because a pair of blacksmiths like us were 'bound to make sparks fly.'

english: I was doing some shopping earlier. Seems Holt has caught wind...
french: Je suis allé faire des courses tout à l'heure. Je crois que Holt a flairé quelque chose...
russian: Я недавно ходил за покупками. Кажется, Хольт о чём-то догадывается...
bulgarian: I was doing some shopping earlier. Seems Holt has caught wind...

english: I wouldn't want you getting heatstroke on me.
french: Je ne voudrais pas que tu aies un coup de chaud.
russian: Не хочу, чтобы у тебя из-за меня случился тепловой удар.
bulgarian: I wouldn't want you getting heatstroke on me.

english: Here, drink this.
french: Tiens, bois ça.
russian: Вот, попей.
bulgarian: Here, drink this.

english: The temperature can get pretty intense near the forge, so be careful, okay?
french: La température est très élevée à côté de la forge, alors fais attention.
russian: Рядом с печью бывает очень жарко, так что будь осторожнее, ладно?
bulgarian: The temperature can get pretty intense near the forge, so be careful, okay?

english: Or get new clothes or something?
french: Ou c'est ta tenue ?
russian: Или одежда новая, или что-то ещё?
bulgarian: Or get new clothes or something?

english: Oh! I thought... nevermind.
french: Oh ! J'aurais cru... Peu importe.
russian: Ой! Я подумал... Не важно.
bulgarian: Oh! I thought... nevermind.

english: I mean, I guess you just look nice today.
french: C'est simplement parce que je te trouve magnifique aujourd'hui.
russian: То есть ты просто хорошо сегодня выглядишь.
bulgarian: I mean, I guess you just look nice today.

english: Uh. Well. More so than usual.
french: Euh. Enfin, comme tous les jours.
russian: Эм. В смысле ещё лучше, чем обычно.
bulgarian: Uh. Well. More so than usual.

english: So... good job.
french: Alors... bravo.
russian: Так что... Молодец.
bulgarian: So... good job.

english: Did you do something new with your hair?
french: Tu as fait quelque chose à tes cheveux ?
russian:
Ты что-то

сделали

сделаласделалсделало с причёской?
bulgarian: Did you do something new with your hair?

english: Well, I run pretty hot... stay close and warm up.
french: Si tu as froid, tu peux venir te réchauffer auprès de moi.
russian: А я как раз так запарился... Иди ко мне, погрейся.
bulgarian: Well, I run pretty hot... stay close and warm up.

english: I mean, if you want.
french: Enfin, si ça te dit.
russian: То есть если хочешь, конечно.
bulgarian: I mean, if you want.

english: It's getting chilly, isn't it?
french: Il fait un peu frais, non ?
russian: Прохладно стало, да?
bulgarian: It's getting chilly, isn't it?
